text: A twenty-five-foot wave of molasses is tearing through Boston.
January, nineteen nineteen. A giant tank by the harbor just burst.
Two point three million gallons. All at once.
It flattens buildings. And the freezing cold makes it worse.
It thickens like glue, and people get stuck.
Twenty-one people die. About a hundred and fifty are hurt.
The harbor stays brown for months.
The tank leaked from day one. Neighbors collected the drips.
The company's fix? They painted it brown... so nobody could see the leaks.
It was never even tested with water.
Then they blamed anarchists. A bomb, they said.
The company was found responsible and paid over six hundred thousand dollars.
After that, Boston made engineers sign off on big structures like it.
And locals swore that on hot summer days, the North End smelled sweet for decades.
Did you learn something new? Like, and subscribe.
